items.title: Allow ignoring apps outside /Applications
items.body:
Fixes #991

Apps outside `/Applications`, such as ones in `~/Applications`, silently fail to add to the ignored apps list.

The app picker uses SwiftUI `fileImporter` and reads the selected app with `Bundle(path:)`. Because Maccy is sandboxed, the URL it gets back is security-scoped, and reading it requires `startAccessingSecurityScopedResource()` first. That call was missing. `/Applications` is readable from the sandbox anyway, so apps there worked. For any other location, `Bundle(path:)` returned `nil` and the selection was dropped with no error.

This change starts access before reading the bundle and stops it afterwards.

How I checked:
- I built a small ad-hoc signed app bundle with Maccy's sandbox entitlements (`app-sandbox` + `files.user-selected.read-only`). Inside it, `Bundle(path:)` returns `com.apple.Safari` for `/Applications/Safari.app` but `nil` for an app in `~/Applications`. Unsandboxed, both return a bundle id.
- The Debug build succeeds and SwiftLint is clean for the changed file.
- I couldn't script the open panel end to end on my machine, so it would be good if someone picks an app from `~/Applications` in the Ignore settings to confirm.

Implemented with Claude Code; I reviewed and tested the change.
